oral_source: PMID 28808905 (Pan 2017, Table 2 of the PMC full text): single 801 mg dose, the clinical dose taken 3 times a day; geometric mean Cmax 6,560 and 7,640 ng/mL fed, 12,500 and 12,600 ng/mL fasted (capsules, tablet). PMID 17906160 (Shi 2007, 200 to 600 mg doses) reports 9.2 mg/L fed and 13.0 mg/L fasted, the same range
eye_source: PMID 21866212: one 50 uL drop of 0.5% pirfenidone on the rabbit eye (250 ug); tissue Cmax in mg/g

skin_gel_dermis_average_estimates.formulation: 8% nanoemulsion gel, pig skin, 404.9 ug/cm2 over 24 h (PMID 33006045)
plain pirfenidone, about 5x below the liposomal gel (PMID 26114208)

blood_flow_assumption: assumption: resting skin gets about 250 mL/min across about 1.8 m2, so about 0.8 mL/h per cm2; the scalp is better perfused, so the range goes up to about 3x that
clinical_topical_evidence: PMID 21659848: 8% gel 3x/day for 6 months improved pediatric hypertrophic burn scars, no serious adverse effects
PMID 25533576: pirfenidone gel in localized scleroderma, phase II
PMID 30115530: topical pirfenidone sped healing of skin graft donor sites
antifibrotic_mechanism_at_clinical_level: PMID 36585256 (Ma 2023, the paper behind GSE226249): pirfenidone inhibits MRTF activation in primary human lung fibroblasts with IC50 50 to 150 uM and > 90% maximal inhibition; patients' peak concentration is < 100 uM
verdict: Neither route clearly reaches the 1 mM cell-culture level as a whole-dermis average (about 0.01 to 0.1 mM by flux / blood flow, the same order as the pill). But the cell-culture level is probably not the bar: the pill slows lung fibrosis in patients at 0.035 to 0.068 mM (the 801 mg dose, fed to fasted), 15 to 28x below it. A gel concentrates drug at the surface and in follicle openings, where the upper-follicle scarring sits (site tissue reached tens of mM on the rabbit eye), and 8% gel has clinical antifibrotic effects in human skin. The real test is a dose-response in human scalp follicles (about 0.03 to 3 mM), which the proposed organ-culture experiment should include.
